name: Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: The fortress town on the Inn with Europe’s largest street organ and a direct view of the Kaisergebirge.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kufstein is the vibrant capital of the Kufstein district in the Tyrolean Unterinntal and, with around 20,000 residents, the second-largest city in Tyrol. Situated at an altitude of 504 metres directly along the green Inn River at the foot of the dramatic Kaiser Mountains, Kufstein is widely known as the "Pearl of Tyrol", celebrated in the famous Kufstein song. The unmistakable city icon is the commanding Kufstein Fortress, perched atop a 90-metre-high rock in the heart of town. Kufstein masterfully combines urban flair, rich history, renowned craftsmanship like Riedel crystal glassware, and immediate alpine recreation in the Kaisergebirge nature reserve.

History

Prehistoric remains in the Tischofer Cave in the Kaisertal demonstrate human habitation dating back 30,000 years to the Paleolithic era. The settlement was first documented in 788 as Caofstein. Owing to its strategic border position between Tyrol and Bavaria, Kufstein was contested for centuries, receiving municipal town rights in 1393. In 1504, Emperor Maximilian I captured the fortress using heavy siege cannons and incorporated Kufstein into Habsburg Tyrol, commissioning the grand Emperor's Tower. With the opening of the Unterinntal Railway in 1858, Kufstein flourished as a vital international trading node. Since 1931, the fortress has housed the famous Heroes' Organ, the world's largest open-air organ with 4,948 pipes.

Getting There

Kufstein is a premier European transport junction along the Munich-Innsbruck-Verona corridor. Kufstein railway station is an international border hub served by ÖBB and DB EuroCity and Railjet trains, alongside Austrian S-Bahn (line S8) and Bavarian regional trains. Motorists reach the city via the A12 Inntal Autobahn using the Kufstein-Nord or Kufstein-Süd exits. Since late 2019, the highway section from the German border to Kufstein-Süd is exempt from Austrian motorway toll vignettes. An efficient urban bus network connects all neighbourhoods and surrounding valley communities.

Tips

Exploring Kufstein Fortress is an absolute must: listen to the daily midday concert on the world's largest outdoor organ resonating across the city, and discover the 60-metre-deep Deep Well and underground rock passages. Stroll through the charming cobbled Römerhofgasse with its traditional frescoed facades, home to the historic Auracher Löchl tavern and the record-holding Stollen 1930 gin bar. Take the nostalgic Kaiserlift single-chair lift from town directly up to Brentenjoch at 1,256 metres in the Kaiser Mountains nature reserve. To witness master craftsmanship, tour the sensory glassmaking demonstration at the Riedel Crystal headquarters.
